html:
SlopSwipe swipes away AI-generated videos while you scroll short videos, using rules you turn on. Every decision is made on your phone. This policy explains what we read, keep and send.

  • On-screen text is checked on your phone and is never uploaded. No screen recording, no screenshots.
  • No account. We don't collect names, email addresses or your advertising ID, and there are no ads.
  • All we send is usage stats, crash reports and broken-detection reports (each can be turned off in Settings), plus anonymous reports if you turn them on.

What the accessibility service reads

SlopSwipe uses Android's accessibility service and works only inside YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels (Instagram stays off until you turn it on in Settings). It reads text on screen: video titles, captions, account names, hashtags and the platform's AI labels, compares them with your rules, and swipes up when one matches.

  • No screen recording or screenshots; no video or audio is read.
  • No comments, messages or login details are read, and it does nothing in other apps.
  • Screen text is processed on the phone and is never uploaded.
  • It never acts on ads or sponsored content.
  • Until you tap "Agree" in the app, it reads nothing, even if the service is switched on.

Data kept only on your phone

DataContentsKept for
Skip and hint historyTime, platform, account name, the rule that matched and the word that matched (such as the platform's AI label or #aigenerated), and whether you undid it, marked it wrong, or how long you watched a hinted video. No full titles or captions30 days, then deleted automatically
Daily countsPer platform and day: videos seen, time on the video feed, skips, hints and undosUntil you delete them
Your lists and rulesBlock list, allow list, your keywords and ignored wordsUntil you delete them
Rule suggestionsHashtags and their counts from videos you marked as AI or undid, used only for the rule suggestions on the home screen. Nothing changes until you accept oneUntil you delete them
My reportsThe anonymous reports you sent and their review status (see section 3)Until you delete them
SettingsYour switches and schedules. With parent mode on, only a salted hash of the PIN is stored, never the PIN itselfUntil you clear the app's storage or uninstall

Everything above except Settings can be deleted at once in Settings → Delete all data. Clearing SlopSwipe's storage in Android settings, or uninstalling the app, deletes your settings too. None of this goes into your Google cloud backup.

The Wellbeing module is on by default and can be turned off in the app at any time. It uses the same daily counts to work out your time and videos on the feeds; its limit, bedtime and focus rules start off, and only after you turn them on does it show a reminder or go back to the home screen. The weekly summary is made on the phone too. Share cards are made on the phone and only leave it through the system share sheet when you choose to share one.

What is sent

The first three are on by default and can each be turned off in Settings → Privacy. Anonymous reports are off by default. Broken-detection reports, daily totals and crash reports are only sent after you accept the disclosure in the app. Usage events are sent from the first time you open the app, so we can see which setup step people get stuck on; turning off Anonymous stats stops them.

ItemContentsWhen it's sent, how long it's kept
Broken-detection report (to our server)Platform, SlopSwipe version, YouTube/TikTok/Instagram app version, rule set version, whether the platform profile was checked on a real phone, read-completeness countsWhen a platform update stops detection; our server keeps only aggregated numbers
Anonymous stats: daily totals (to our server)Date, SlopSwipe version, skip/hint/undo counts per platform, whether setup was finishedAt most once a day; our server keeps only aggregated numbers
Anonymous stats: usage events (Google Firebase Analytics)Which step you took in the app, such as finishing setup, accepting the disclosure, turning the service on, skipping or undoing a video, or opening a page, with only parameters like the platform and rule code; a few setting values (sensitivity, which platforms are on, whether Wellbeing and the service are on); and a random identifier Firebase creates for this installation (app instance ID). Firebase also records the app version, device model, Android version, language, time spent in the app, and an approximate location (country or region) Google derives from a masked IP address. No screen content, account names, keywords you typed or advertising IDSent in batches as things happen; kept in Google Analytics for 2 months
Crash report (Google Firebase Crashlytics)The error and code location, SlopSwipe version, device model, Android version, memory and storage state, and a random identifier Firebase creates for this installation (Firebase installation ID)Next launch after a crash; Crashlytics keeps it for 90 days. Turning crash reports off also deletes reports not yet sent
Anonymous reports (off by default; you turn them on)Platform, the creator account you report, the reason ("this is AI" or "wrong call"), the rule codes that matched, your own undo-rate range (low/mid/high), and a random report ID your phone creates when you opt inWhen you tap "This is AI", or mark a list-based skip as wrong; kept until you delete them

Anonymous reports contain only the public creator account you reported: not your own account, screen content or any personal data. The random report ID only lets you see your reports' status and lets reviewers tell repeated reports from one person apart. Delete every report under that ID from our server in Settings → My reports → Delete report data. Broken-detection reports and daily totals carry no identifier at all, and our server does not store IP addresses.

The Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics identifiers are used only inside SlopSwipe and are replaced when you reinstall; we can't use them to find out who you are. Google handles both under Firebase's privacy and security terms. Once you turn one off nothing more is sent, and what was already sent is deleted when the retention period above ends. All data is sent over HTTPS and stored in Google Firebase (Google Cloud).

Downloads the app needs

The app downloads a digitally signed rule set (keywords, lists, screen layouts) from our server from time to time; no data about you is sent with it. It also fetches a few remote settings (such as how often to ask for a rating) from Google Firebase Remote Config; that request carries the Firebase installation ID, app version, Android version, country and language codes and time zone, and nothing else. These two can't be turned off, and neither sends anything about how you use the app.

Creator appeals

Creators can ask for their account to be taken off the user-reported list on the appeal page. An appeal keeps the platform, account, explanation and any contact detail you choose to leave (used only to reply, never published). Outcomes (account, result, date) are published on the appeal page.

Permissions

PermissionWhat it's for
Accessibility serviceReads on-screen text on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram video feeds and swipes up when a rule matches (section 1)
Network (INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE)Downloads the rule set and sends the data in section 3; checks for a connection before sending
Notifications (POST_NOTIFICATIONS; Android 13 and later asks you)Alerts when the service is turned off, detection stops working on a platform, SlopSwipe is paused, and the weekly summary
Checking specific apps (queries)Only checks whether YouTube, TikTok and Instagram are installed and which version, to pick the right platform profile. It can't see any other app on your phone
Google Play install referrer (BIND_GET_INSTALL_REFERRER_SERVICE)Added by Firebase Analytics; reads which Google Play source the app was installed from
WAKE_LOCKAdded by Android's background scheduler (WorkManager) so background jobs can finish: deleting expired history daily, checking for rule updates and making the weekly summary. SlopSwipe has no permission to start when the phone boots, so after a restart these jobs resume the next time you open the app

SlopSwipe deliberately removes the advertising ID permissions Firebase would add (AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION), so it can't read your advertising ID.

Google Play

When you get SlopSwipe from Google Play, Google handles install and payment data under its own policies and gives developers aggregated statistics such as installs, ratings and crash rates; we can't see individual users. The rating prompt in the app is an official Google Play card. Your stars and review are posted publicly on Google Play under your Google account, and we aren't told who left them.

What we don't do

  • No account; no names, emails or contact details (except a contact a creator chooses to leave with an appeal).
  • No advertising or attribution SDKs. Google Firebase is used only for crash reports (Crashlytics), anonymous usage events (Analytics) and remote settings (Remote Config). We don't sell data or share it with third parties; Google processes this data on our behalf as a service provider.
  • No AI model decides what to skip; only fixed rules you can see and turn off.

Children

SlopSwipe is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect their personal data. If you believe a child's data was sent to us, email us and we'll delete it.

Changes and contact

Material changes will be announced in the app and on this page, and the effective date above will change. Questions or deletion requests: feedback@dapplebyte.com
